name: tool-call
title: Tool call
purpose: A summary of one tool call outside a transcript: the tool, its target, how it ended and how long it took, with the arguments and output behind disclosures.
whenToUse: In an activity view or a run's detail view, to show one tool call on its own or a short list of them.
When the reader needs the outcome of a call first and its arguments and output only on request.
whenNotToUse: For a tool call as a row of a transcript. Use a message of the tool-call kind, with a tool-result message after it.
For a call that still waits for the reader's answer. Use an approval, which carries Allow and Decline.
For a one-line record of what an agent did, among other events. Use an activity feed entry.

variants.name: succeeded
variants.use: The call returned without an error. The status reads Succeeded beside a check icon.

variants.name: failed
variants.use: The call ran and returned an error. The status reads Failed beside an alert icon, and gw-tool-call__note says what failed.

variants.name: denied
variants.use: The call was refused by the reader or by a permission rule and did not run. The status reads Denied beside a ban icon, and gw-tool-call__note says what was not run and why.

accessibility: Use an article with aria-labelledby pointing at gw-tool-call__title, a heading. Its level is the one under the heading it sits beneath: h2 directly under the view's h1, h3 inside a section headed by an h2. In a queue or a list every title takes the same level. The class sets the size, so the level changes nothing on screen. The title holds the tool name and then the target, both as text.
Several calls are li elements of a ul or ol, one article in each.
gw-tool-call__status always holds the status as a word: Running, Succeeded, Failed or Denied. The stylesheet draws the icon from the variant class, so the status is never colour alone.

While the call runs, set aria-busy="true" on the article and leave the variant class off. When it ends, remove aria-busy, add the variant class and change the word. Announce the change from a role="status" element in the view when the reader is waiting on it.
Write the duration with its unit, such as 2.4 s or 48 s so far. A duration that ticks is not in a live region.

Arguments and output each go in a native details element whose summary says what is inside and how long it is, such as Output, 6 lines. They start closed. Enter and Space open and close a summary, and its pointer target is 44px tall.
Write arguments and output as text, never as markup, and write out characters that cannot be seen. gw-tool-call__code wraps and never scrolls sideways.
It holds no action. The component needs no script: the app sets aria-busy, the variant class and the text.
